text: The ultrasound findings suggest a cystic mass causing biliary obstruction, which could be a choledochal cyst or a cystic neoplasm. I need to visualize the anatomy more clearly to distinguish between benign and malignant causes. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP is surprising given the ultrasound findings, so I need to clarify if the "anechoic mass" was actually the dilated gallbladder itself. speaker: Doctor
text: It is highly unusual for the CT to be normal given the ultrasound findings of bile duct dilation, so I must verify if there is a transient obstruction. Have you had any recent episodes of severe right upper quadrant pain or jaundice that resolved on its own? REQUEST TEST: ERCP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ERCP and CT scan effectively rule out mechanical obstruction, suggesting the jaundice is not due to a physical blockage. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal biopsy and imaging, the discrepancy suggests the initial ultrasound finding was a red herring, likely a fluid-filled gallbladder rather than a mass. Since you have significant weight loss and jaundice with no obstructive or inflammatory cause, have you experienced any changes in your bowel habits such as fatty stools or diarrhea? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Elastase

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of painless jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine in an elderly male, along with ultrasound evidence of biliary dilation that may have been obscured or misinterpreted by subsequent normal imaging, this is highly suggestive of a malignancy at the head of the pancreas or ampulla of Vater. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Cancer
